gap: No result ChatGPT got states what each dollar buys in battery or keys: on the makers' own listings the ATK A87 gives about 400 mAh per dollar against the Royal Kludge RK61's 29, and the 101-key Gamakay TK101 costs about $0.48 a key against the RK61's $0.82.
standout_why: Compared against mkbguide.com and rottenwifi.com (both cited), official.deals/under-50 and mechvibes.com, all opened 2026-11-21. Rottenwifi and mechvibes give the RK61's 1,450 mAh and $49.99 but never divide them; mkbguide gives no prices and one battery figure (Redragon K556, 1,600 mAh); official.deals gives prices and two capacities with no ratio. None states battery hours, days per charge, mAh per dollar or cost per key. It scores 1, not 2, because the inputs are partly on those pages and ChatGPT's own answer already quotes the A87's 12,000 mAh. The stronger figure, work-days per charge from each maker's rated hours, could not be built: every maker product page returned HTTP 429 and Newegg returned 403.
decides: It confirms ChatGPT's pick and does not change it: the ATK A87 leads on both battery per dollar and price per key among the boards I could source, and atk.store listed it at $29.98 today, below the $34.98 ChatGPT showed. For our row, the Gamakay TK101 at $47.99 honestly wins one segment: the only board in this set with a number pad under $50 (101 keys, maker's count), at about $0.48 a key. The comparison is incomplete, because battery capacity for the TK101, NS68, K530 Pro and K526 Pro was not readable, so battery per dollar covers only the A87 and RK61.
